structure_gain: IRIS+GPT-4 detects 55/120 vulnerabilities vs CodeQL's 27/120, F1 0.177 vs 0.076 (Table 1); this compares the full neurosymbolic taint-context pipeline against a static-only baseline, not the same model with/without structure.
confound_note: Central comparison is IRIS (LLM-inferred taint specs + static dataflow engine) vs CodeQL alone (no LLM) -- both model and analysis method differ simultaneously, so representation is not isolated. A secondary ablation (Table 3) swaps LLM- vs CodeQL-derived source/sink specs.
stop_detail: LLM-inferred taint specifications (source/sink/sanitizer/propagator) populate an inter-procedural dataflow graph; detected source-to-sink code paths are serialized with surrounding +/-5 lines for contextual LLM analysis (Sec 3.1-3.5, Appendix A.3).
threats_to_datum: Numbers taken from the paper's own tables/figures across a multi-revision preprint (v3); GPT-4 API version and exact CodeQL configuration not independently verified by extractor.

venue: arXiv (preprint; stated to appear in IEEE conference proceedings, specific venue unconfirmed)
structure_gain: Removing RAG context (holding GPT-4o and CoT fixed) drops F1 from 33.49% to 23.92%, a 9.57pp loss (Table III).
confound_note: Table III ablation varies retrieval context and CoT prompting independently while holding the GPT-4o model fixed -- a genuine representation-only ablation for the RAG factor; Table II comparison to VulDeePecker/Reveal changes model and method entirely.
stop_detail: Input code is embedded via OpenAI embeddings; top-5 cosine-similar CWE/CVE examples are retrieved from a 500-instance Big-Vul vector store (ChromaDB); GPT-4o selects the best-matching exemplar to ground its classification (RAG formula, Sec III).
threats_to_datum: 5-page short preprint; single-run reported numbers with no confidence intervals or variance; retrieval corpus drawn from the same Big-Vul dataset used for evaluation, raising potential train/retrieval-test leakage concerns.

key_numbers.value: MoCQ 77.4% vs DSL0 (no spec) 9.9% vs DSL100 50.0%

structure_gain: Providing a subset DSL grammar (MoCQ) instead of no specification raises query-generation pass rate from 9.9% (DSL0) to 77.4%, and F1 from 0.31 (DSL100, full grammar) to 0.51 (MoCQ), same LLM loop (Tables 7-8).
confound_note: The DSL0/DSL100/MoCQ ablation varies only the amount/form of structured grammar given to the same iterative LLM loop -- a clean representation-only ablation; the SOTA comparison (Table 4, vs Pure LLM/GRACE/KNighter/IRIS) also changes analysis architecture entirely.
stop_detail: LLM iteratively generates CPG/CodeQL queries from a BNF-grammar DSL spec, receiving symbolic-validator feedback (syntax/runtime/semantic errors) and intermediate program states after each query block, refining over up to 20 iterations (Algorithm 1).
threats_to_datum: Numbers span multiple ablation tables (2, 4, 7, 8) in a still-revised preprint (v5, 2026); CPG/CodeQL backend differs per language, which may confound the cross-language comparison.

venue: EASE 2025 (28th->29th International Conference on Evaluation and Assessment in Software Engineering, ACM proceedings, Istanbul)

key_numbers.metric: repair rate per run (Short+CVE+Manual vs GPT-4o baseline)
avg repair rate, CWE vs CVE context
Top-3 prompt ensemble, distinct vulns fixed
key_numbers.value: 26/42 (61.9%) vs original baseline 17/42 (40.4%) vs GPT-4o reproduction 19/42 (45.2%)

structure_gain: Combining a CVE-derived repair guideline with manually extracted repository context (Short+CVE Hints+Manual) achieves the best single-prompt result (18-14-17 across 3 runs) vs GPT-4o baseline (11-12-14), same GPT-4o-2024-08-06 model, temperature 0.01 throughout (Table 1).
confound_note: The central ablation (Table 1) holds the LLM (GPT-4o) and temperature fixed while varying only prompt context content (code visibility, docs, CWE, CVE, manual hints) -- a clean representation-only ablation; the separate GPT-4 vs GPT-4o comparison confounds model version with non-identical evaluation methodology (Sec 5).
stop_detail: Manually curated context -- class headers, redacted-but-named referenced methods, imports, standardized CWE text, raw/GPT-summarized CVE descriptions, and manually identified project-specific hints -- is inserted directly into a zero-shot prompt (Sec 3.2-3.3, Table 1).
threats_to_datum: Authors' own stated threats: Java-only generalizability, GPT-4o non-determinism even at temp 0.01, manual context extraction introduces subjectivity, and the GPT-4 vs GPT-4o comparison used non-identical evaluation methodology (Sec 5).

venue: arXiv ("submitted to the IEEE for possible publication"; not yet accepted anywhere -- note: an initial abstract-only fetch incorrectly suggested IEEE S&P 2025 acceptance, which full text does not support)
datasets: custom dataset: 25 GitHub repositories (~250K LOC, Python/Java/JavaScript), authors' own ground truth of 170 vulnerabilities
structure_gain: SAST-Genius (fine-tuned LLM + structured AST/taint-path JSON prompt) reaches 89.5% precision vs Semgrep's 35.7% (no LLM) and GPT-4's 65.5% (Table 1), but model, fine-tuning, and representation all differ simultaneously across arms.
confound_note: Table 1's three-way comparison (Semgrep vs GPT-4 vs SAST-Genius) varies representation, base model, and fine-tuning status all at once -- not a representation-only ablation; no experiment holds the model fixed while toggling only the AST/taint-path context.
stop_detail: Semgrep's intermediate representations (AST nodes and source-to-sink taint paths) plus call-graph/library-dependency context and the original rule/severity are serialized into a structured JSON prompt fed to a fine-tuned Llama-3-8B triage engine, which outputs a verdict plus reasoning summary (Sec III.A, Fig. 1).
threats_to_datum: Evaluation dataset (25 GitHub repos, ground truth via manual expert review) is a custom, unreleased dataset built by the authors -- selection/labeling bias risk; unreviewed preprint explicitly "submitted to IEEE for possible publication" (not accepted); authors disclose using ChatGPT/Gemini for writing assistance; fine-tuning data partly proprietary and undisclosed.

venue: FLLM2025 (3rd International Conference on Foundation and Large Language Models)
datasets: Draper VDISC-derived labeled snippets (Russell et al. 2018), 4 CWE categories: CWE-119/120/469/476

key_numbers.value: Fine-tuned Gemini-1.5-Flash 59.31% F1 vs Fine-tuned CodeBERT 91.22% F1

structure_gain: Retrieval-augmented 20-shot prompting raises F1 from 36.35% (zero-shot) to 74.05%, same Gemini-1.5-Flash model (Table I) -- retrieval of semantically similar labeled examples is the sole varied factor across the few-shot arms.
confound_note: Few-shot arms (random vs retrieval-augmented vs retrieval-based labeling) hold the base model fixed and vary only the example-selection mechanism -- a clean representation-only ablation; the separate fine-tuned CodeBERT/Gemini comparisons change both model and training paradigm.
stop_detail: Query code is embedded via gemini-embedding-001; top-k semantically similar labeled code+vulnerability-label pairs are retrieved via cosine similarity from a ChromaDB store and inserted as few-shot exemplars in the prompt (retrieval mechanism section).
threats_to_datum: Dataset restricted to 4 CWE categories from a single source (Russell et al. 2018), limiting generalizability; only one base LLM (Gemini-1.5-Flash) tested across the prompting arms.

key_numbers.value: MulVul 34.79% vs GPT-4o 3.86% vs LLM x CPG 24.58% vs LLMVulExp 22.72% vs VISION 18.12%

structure_gain: Removing retrieval-augmentation alone (agents/base LLM held fixed) drops Macro-F1 from 34.56% to 21.80%, a 30.7pp loss (Table 4) -- a clean representation-only ablation isolating the retrieved vulnerability-knowledge-base context.
confound_note: Main SOTA comparison (Table 2, vs GPT-4o/LLM x CPG/LLMVulExp/VISION) changes architecture, model, and representation simultaneously; only the internal Table 4 ablation isolates retrieval while holding agents/LLM fixed.
stop_detail: Router and Detector agents call retrieval tools to pull evidence from vulnerability knowledge bases (CWE/pattern databases) during multi-agent coarse-to-fine classification, grounding predictions to reduce hallucination (retrieval-augmented multi-agent framework section, Table 4 ablation).
threats_to_datum: Evaluated only on PrimeVul (C/C++); authors themselves flag generalizability to other languages as unexplored; numbers from a v1 arXiv preprint, not yet peer reviewed; one baseline (LLM x CPG) is itself GNN-assisted, complicating a like-for-like comparison.

datasets: NIST-SARD (105 memory-focused vulnerable samples, 15 CWE types)

key_numbers.value: Structural Integrity ~7.5/10, Ground Truth Alignment ~6.14/10, Code Reasoning ~7.32/10, Remediation Quality ~6.98/10
70 Google Project Zero reports + 1,321 CWE entries

structure_gain: none reported (no RAG-vs-no-RAG ablation; single-system LLM-judge quality scores only, no unstructured/raw-text baseline comparator)
confound_note: No baseline or ablation is reported at all -- the 54.21% quality score is not compared against any raw-text-only or no-retrieval configuration, so the retrieval contribution cannot be isolated (paper states no RAG-vs-non-RAG ablation is provided).
stop_detail: A RAG engine embeds and retrieves from 70 Google Project Zero root-cause-analysis reports and 1,321 MITRE CWE entries using vector similarity, BM25-hybrid, or HyPE (hypothetical-question) retrieval, feeding passages to the Analyst/Reporter agents that draft the vulnerability report.
threats_to_datum: Quality metric is an LLM-judge score, not a standard detection/repair metric, and no baseline/ablation isolates the retrieval contribution; task is report-generation rather than detection/localization/repair proper; title claims binary-program analysis but evaluation covers only source-code samples from NIST-SARD -- a scope mismatch between claimed and demonstrated capability.

stop_detail: Agent tools return file content with line numbers, ripgrep-based regex search, and Iter_grep (parses the repository AST to locate definitions/use-sites, ranked by proximity to the error location); History-Fix/Security-Pattern/Refinement-Trajectory memories retrieve prior fixes, defense patterns, and failure trajectories to ground each repair attempt.
threats_to_datum: Paper contains an unresolved LaTeX template placeholder ("Conference: Make sure to enter the correct conference title"), indicating an unfinished/unedited preprint; cost and resolution numbers are single-run, self-reported figures across three benchmarks with differing baseline model configurations.

venue: Internetware 2026 ("Accepted for presentation", per arXiv comments field)

key_numbers.value: >93% of tokens offloaded to the lightweight Explorer agent

structure_gain: DREA's on-demand repository exploration raises Pair-Correctness from a function-only baseline (19-26% across three LLMs) to 30-42% with DREA (Table 1).
confound_note: Paper explicitly notes its baselines (Function-Only, Whole-File, Single-Agent) conflate representation (amount of code seen) with exploration strategy (tool access, planner/explorer decoupling), so the reported gains are not a clean representation-only ablation.
stop_detail: The lightweight Explorer agent uses read-only repo tools (ls, glob, grep, read_file) to gather Repository Context, Code Evidence, and Security Findings on demand, reporting back to the Planning agent, which forms and refines vulnerability hypotheses (Planner-Explorer architecture section).
threats_to_datum: RepoPairBench is small (100 vulnerability-fix pairs / 200 instances) and Python-only, with C/C++ extension left as future work; the pair-correctness metric requires both vulnerable and fixed versions to be classified correctly, a stricter and less standard metric than typical F1/precision, complicating cross-paper comparison.
